pairsNote: Documented pairing: each tinted neutral goes with the accents of its hue family; gray goes with any accent. bronze and gold have no documented neutral; use sand or gray.

status.note: Fill (solid badge, dot, bar): the contrast.accent.<scale>.fill step for the current mode with white text (all five statuses resolve to white on-fill); text on neutral surfaces: step 11 (step 12 if 11 < 4.5:1); subtle badge background: step 3, border: step 6. Never by colour alone: pair with an icon or label.

finance/payments.avoid: green as brand (reads as gain), red accents

e-commerce.avoid: small orange text on light surfaces

devtools.avoid: decorative neon, terminal green as brand

energy/IoT.avoid: status green clashing with brand green: shift one

real estate/property.avoid: loud saturated brand fills over listings and photos

insurance.avoid: red accents (reads as claim denied or alarm)

travel/hospitality.avoid: cold grey chrome, amber text on light surfaces

food/restaurant.avoid: red as an error cue next to the brand red

crypto/web3.avoid: neon purple gradients, glow effects, rocket imagery

media/content.avoid: many category colours competing with imagery

agriculture/farming.avoid: lime text on light surfaces, toy-like greens

manufacturing/industrial.avoid: yellow text on light surfaces, hazard-stripe decoration

fitness/wellness.avoid: neon gradients, shaming red for missed goals

construction/field-ops.avoid: orange status colours colliding with the brand orange

contrast.note: WCAG 2.x ratios floored to 1 decimal (never rounded up); l=light, d=dark. s11OnS1, s11OnS2 and s12OnS2 are measured on step 1 and step 2 of the paired neutral (palettes.pairs; bronze and gold use sand); the surface is step 2. whiteFillStep = lowest step (9,10,11) that passes 4.5:1 with white on the light scale. fill.<mode> = {fill: step, fillHex, onFill, ratio}: the step to use for filled controls in that mode, chosen by the legibility rule (white text stays; if white on step 9 is under 4.5:1 the fill moves to the first of steps 10, 11, 8, 7 that passes). onFill is white for every scale; dark text is never used on a mid-tone or dark fill.

tailwindMeta.note: hex converted from the package oklch values (sRGB, rounded)

legibility: Foreground must be clearly visible: light text on dark surfaces, dark text on light surfaces; any text/background pair under 3:1 is a bug.
Body text needs 4.5:1; text >= 24px (or bold >= 18.66px) and UI components need 3:1.
Filled controls (primary button, solid badge, active nav, selected chip) use white text by default, in light and dark mode.
If white on step 9 is under 4.5:1, keep the hue and move the fill to the first step that passes 4.5:1 with white, searching 10, 11, 8, 7; record it as fill.
Dark text on a fill only when the fill itself is genuinely light (luminance >= 0.4 and white fails by a wide margin); prefer a darker step with white.
Hover/active/disabled re-check the pair (hover keeps 4.5:1, disabled stays >= 3:1); never accent step-11 text on a same-hue subtle background under 4.5:1, use step 12.
Use at most two non-page zones (brand, ink) on one screen; the rest stays on the page zone.
A saturated brand zone is for chrome and hero bands (sidebar, header, banner), never for data surfaces; keep it off tables and charts.
Chart and table data always sit on page or surface zones, not on brand or ink zones.

taxonomy: Detection: each domain lists lowercase `keywords`. The scan (or the agent) counts whole-word hits (plural and -ing/-ed variants allowed) in the page title and h1 (weight 3), nav labels (weight 2) and the remaining text (weight 1), picks the domain with the highest score, and falls back to `general admin` when confidence (top score over total score) is under 0.25 or the top score is under 2. The chosen domain gives `accent`, `neutral` and three `combos` (calm, paper, brand). A known brand colour overrides the accent: keep its hue, pick the nearest scale, and take the paired neutral from `pairs`.
zonesNote: Zones: page = the working surface (data lives here), brand = the accent as a whole surface with light foreground (sidebar, header or hero band), ink = a dark neutral surface with light foreground (sidebar, code or hero block). Every combo defines the three zones in light and dark; `ratios` holds measured WCAG ratios floored to 1 decimal, all >= 4.5. Paper uses a tinted step of a warm or tinted neutral instead of pure white. All colours come from `scales`, plus #ffffff.
